title: NFL today: How to watch Rams v Broncos, TV channels & live stream Sunday 27 September - The Guardian
content: How will the Rams and Broncos fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream options The Rams may have just needed a change in continent. The preseason Super Bowl favorites briefly surrendered that status after going to Australia in Week 1 and falling flat against their NFC West rivals, the 49ers. Playing in Melbourne, the Rams lost the time of possession battle 36 minutes to 24, gained fewer than 300 yards of offense, and lost a 27-7 decision. “Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn, and you know, sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that put you in a bad spot,” coach Sean McVay cracked last week. He could afford to be lighthearted because the Rams had just righted the ship on Monday Night Football, shellacking the visiting Giants by a nearly equivalent score of 28-6. MVP Matthew Stafford looked like himself, legendary defensive tackle Aaron Donald rejoined the lineup, and all was well again in Los Angeles. Another challenge awaits in Denver, where the Broncos rebounded from their own Week 1 disaster (a 31-10 loss to the Chiefs) to beat a solid Jaguars team last Sunday. Last year’s top seed in the AFC playoffs, the Broncos have QB Bo Nix back from a right ankle fracture suffered during that run. The two teams will get together at Mile High for their first meeting since a 51-14 Rams rout in December 2022. Stadium: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver, Colorado) United States: Watch on NBC or Peacock; Stream on Fubo Nix is back, but the Broncos need him to find his sea legs. Through two weeks, a tiny sample, Nix is 26th in the NFL in passer rating and 24th in adjusted net yards per attempt. He’s thrown an interception in both of his games. But his stats are mainly weighed down by a horrendous Week 1, and Nix may have found something (or someone) important in Week 2: Newly acquired wideout Jaylen Waddle took off like a missile and caught eight balls on 10 targets for 138 yards. Waddle appears to be ready to take the No 1 receiver role from one of the team’s longtime stars, the consistent Courtland Sutton. The Rams will expect the usual excellence from Stafford and the offense. A fascinating subplot will be Donald, the future first-ball Hall of Famer who returned on the defensive line last week after being retired during the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Donald played 33 snaps as he worked his way back into game condition, and now he gets to play a game in Denver’s thin air. He made one solo tackle (and one tackle for loss) in his return game. One would expect it to only be up from here for the 35-year-old.

title: RTÉ explains decision for reduced coverage of Republic of Ireland v Israel in Nations League - Yahoo Sports
content: The Republic of Ireland vs Israel in the Nations League will have reduced coverage with the national broadcaster with the build-up making it one of the world's most controversial fixtures. Heimir Hallgrimsson's side are in Debrecen, Hungary for their away game against Israel before a home game in Serbia next Sunday. After calls to boycott both fixtures against a country found by the United Nations independent international commission of committing genocide in Gaza, the game will go ahead, though goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew, citing opposition "against the atrocities in the region." And Irish national public service broadcaster RTÉ has taken steps to alter its usual coverage of the national team. A statement from the broadcaster read: "RTÉ will meet its contractual obligations to broadcast the two Uefa Nations League fixtures between Ireland and Israel. The broadcast arrangement for the two games will be as follows: Commentary will be taken from the international feed and will not be provided by an RTÉ commentator RTÉ has not taken advertising or sponsorship around either game There will be news coverage of the games and the wider events surrounding them "These arrangement reflect RTÉ'S decision to fulfil its contractual broadcasting obligations while limiting the additional production and commercial activity associated with the fixtures."

title: Joel Embiid’s Best Playoff Games, Part V: Game 7 vs Boston in 2026 - Liberty Ballers
content: ﻿Embiid’s return in the middle of the series was capped with a fantastic effort in the decider. Add Liberty Ballers as a preferred source to see more of our reporting on Google. Embiid’s stat line: 34 points, 12 rebounds, 6 assists, 12-of-26 FGs, 1-of-4 3PTs, 1 block, +11 rating Is it a bit much to say Sixers fans were confident heading into this Game 7? Maybe it is given Philadelphia’s reputation as postseason choke artists that was built up in the Embiid era. However, the Sixers had all the momentum in their opening round series against Boston this past spring heading into the decisive game. They had already won twice at TD Garden, including Game 2 in convincing fashion without Embiid. Their victory in Game 6 was a dominant performance that left no doubt they could win the series, a stunning turn of events from a Game 4 blowout loss that saw them go down 3-1 in the series. Then, Jayson Tatum was ruled out for the Celtics just before tipoff. Things were building towards a seminal moment for both Embiid and the entire organization. Everyone knew this was more than just a first-round playoff series given the opponent and the deficit the Sixers were looking to overcome. Once the game started, it looked like Game 6 had never ended. The Sixers led 32-19 after one quarter and unsurprisingly, Embiid dominated the first 12 minutes. The big man had 10 of his 34 points in the first period and it was clear that he was making a concerted effort to score in the paint where Boston didn’t have an answer for him. After playing all 12 minutes of the first quarter, Embiid did take a brief rest in the second quarter, but the Sixers still led by five points at halftime, an outcome they certainly would have signed up for at the beginning of the game. The second quarter also featured a signature defensive play for Embiid who had his lone block just prior to halftime on Jaylen Brown. He only played about half of the third quarter, but Embiid was very efficient coming out of the locker room going 3-of-4 from the field in the quarter and getting five of his 12 rebounds in the seven minutes of action he got in the third. Of course, his scoring efforts were consistent, but it was the rebounding and passing in this one that really made it feel special for Embiid. He was involving his teammates, denying the Celtics of lots of second chances and the rest of the team was rallying behind him. The game was also remembered for the horrendous shooting of the Celtics as Boston went a pitiful 13-of-49 from the three-point line. In typical Sixers fashion, the team found a way to quickly wash away the rally from 3-1 down against Boston by getting swept out of the second round against the Knicks in the following series. However, with a highly-anticipated 2026-27 starting soon, now feels like a good time to remember the best moment of the 2025-26 season, Embiid’s finest thus far as a Sixer. Coming off a career year and his first All-NBA honor, Tyrese Maxey could be even more effective and efficient on these new-look Sixers. The Sixers made a couple huge splashes, but they also fortified their depth. Anyone asking this question about this year’s Sixers is focused on the wrong thing. VJ Edgecombe set the bar high for himself in year one, but there’s a lot of room — and opportunity — for growth ahead in his sophomore season. Inadequate preflight planning, poor preflight inspection, and an attempt to take off above a Cessna Citation V’s mtow with snow-contaminated wings led to a runway overrun on Dec. 27, 2024 at Stevens Field Airport (KPSO) in Pagosa Springs, Colorado, according to a newly released NTSB final report. The overweight condition and contaminated wings likely kept the airplane from rotating at the pilot's calculated speed, and by the time she rejected the takeoff, the airplane was already above decision speed. The planned Part 91 flight was bound for Tulsa Riverside Airport (KRVS) in Oklahoma, but ended when the airplane ran off the end of Runway 1 at KPSO. The light jet ran into the grass, damaging both wings; the two pilots and eight passengers were not injured. According to the NTSB, the pilot's type rating required a qualified second-in-command (SIC), but the copilot held no such rating and, by his own account, did not meet the requirements to act as SIC. The pilot told investigators that she was aware the copilot had no flight experience in type but assumed he was properly trained based on his job at a flight simulator training provider. The airplane’s lease agreement required the lessee, a passenger aboard the flight, to hire “professionally trained and qualified” pilots. But according to the lessee, the management company that operated the airplane, Metroplex Flight Services, arranged the pilots itself and asked only for a passenger count, never for passenger or baggage weights. Passengers told NTSB investigators that the flight crew filled every exterior luggage compartment, loaded a stroller into the lavatory and a child’s car seat into an empty passenger seat, and let each passenger keep a personal bag at their seat. The pilot calculated weight using ForeFlight’s standard average passenger weights—205, 184, and 87 pounds respectively for men, women, and children—for the five men, four women, and one child aboard, plus an estimated 130 pounds of baggage in the rear compartment and 110 pounds in the nose, arriving at a calculated payload of 1,285 pounds. Weights for each bag were determined by “heaviness,” not scales, the NTSB said. The pilot told investigators the airplane’s takeoff weight was about 15,700 pounds, equal to mtow. After the accident, a passenger gave investigators additional figures, including about 100 pounds of luggage inside the cabin and roughly 240 pounds for three dogs aboard, bringing the total reported weight of people, animals, and baggage to 2,154 pounds. Using that information, investigators calculated the airplane’s actual takeoff weight at about 16,502 pounds, some 600 pounds over the 15,900-pound takeoff weight, with the center of gravity near its forward limit and likely outside the operating envelope. The pilot said she performed a standard preflight inspection and noticed only liquid water on the wings, with no icing or other contamination. Airport surveillance video, however, showed snow already accumulating on the wings as the pilot and copilot walked out to the airplane, and continuing to fall as passengers boarded. One passenger said FBO personnel, working with a handheld brush because the airport had no deicing capability, cleared the wings three separate times over about 11 minutes. According to the copilot, the pilot performed a tactile check of the wings after all passengers were loaded, but video showed no such check on the airplane’s right wing—the only wing visible on camera—after the final snow removal. Contamination remained visible on the wings as the airplane began taxiing, the ramp pavement was wet, and the snowfall rate appeared to increase once the airplane left the ramp. About 20 minutes passed between the last time snow was brushed from the wings and the start of the takeoff roll. The report cited FAA Advisory Circular 135-17, which states that snow or frost can reduce wing lift by as much as 30% and increase drag by 40%. The pilot gave conflicting accounts of what followed. She initially said the airplane accelerated normally through the 96-knot decision speed and 103-knot rotation speed, but did not rotate despite full aft deflection of the control yoke. Later, she told investigators that the airplane did not seem to accelerate at the expected rate. Data downloaded by the NTSB from the airplane’s Garmin GTN 750 avionics units showed it reached 120 knots indicated airspeed and 138 knots ground speed before the pilot rejected the takeoff with maximum braking and full reverse thrust. That is above the speed that FAA guidance describes as “the maximum speed by which a rejected takeoff must be initiated to assure that a safe stop can be completed within the remaining runway.” The airplane ran off the end of the runway, continued into the grass, and pivoted left before stopping. Passengers and crew exited and were met by airport emergency personnel. A post-accident examination found no evidence of pre-accident flight-control or engine anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
